messages.subject: peptide PTM annotation and sequence
parts:
Dear all,

Something I have been wondering about: for some of the tools I would like to use following MSstatsPTM analysis, such as PTM-SEA or KinSwingR, I need the (centered) amino acid sequence surrounding the PTM site and the exact location of the PTM on the protein. However, this doesn't seem to be included in the output. Is there a way to achieve this with MSstatsPTM? Or perhaps an existing package that could be used to perform this mapping? 


Kind regards,

Robin Colpaert

messages.author: 6597c45f2a31b5d0
messages.subject: Re: peptide PTM annotation and sequence
parts:
Hi Robin,

I know that the output of the function "groupComparisonPTM" contains the exact location of the PTM on the protein (e.g. if you see Q9UHD8_K262 in the protein column, this  means that lysine was modified at site 262 for protein Q9UHD8).  

To get the centered amino acid sequence surrounding the PTM site, my first thought is that you can download a FASTA file from Uniprot containing all of the proteins of interest in your dataset.  MSstatsPTM has a function called "tidyFasta" which takes your FASTA file and imports it as a data table containing the sequence for each protein.  Then, you can find the amino acid sequence surrounding the PTM site using some additional R code.  

Here's a code example below with Q9UHD8_K262:

library(dplyr)
fasta_data_table = tidyFasta("fasta filepath")
fasta_row = filter(fasta_data_table, uniprot_ac == "Q9UHD8")
amino_acid_sequence = substring(fasta_row$sequence, 257, 267) # taking the 10 amino acids surrounding K262.

In summary, MSstatsPTM does not completely support your situation out of the box, but there's ways to write R code to make this work seamlessly.  Let me know if you have any other questions or need any additional clarifications.

Thanks,
Tony

messages.author: 3cbc02caaeab0f45
messages.subject: Re: peptide PTM annotation and sequence
parts:
Dear Tony,

Thank you for looking into my question! 

I took another look at my data but my output does not look like your example. While the example output in the manual indeed looks like this, my output of groupComparisonPTM however has this format:  sp|A2AAJ9|OBSCN_MOUSE_KASLKDSGEYTCETEASK_[3] Phospho (ST). I added a screenshot in attach to give more examples. 

As far as I can see, my output has the location of the PTMs not in relation to the full protein, but to the short peptide that is mentioned there. Thus I would need a way to first map the location of the PTM in the full protein first. Is there a standard way/existing package that does this, or would I have to do this from scratch starting from the FASTA file? I guess I could grep the specific substring (peptide) in the protein sequence and find it like that? 

Note that I started from progenesis input and thus used the ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat function, while the manual starts from something like MaxQuant. I'm guessing this is the source of the issue? 

EDIT: just before sending this I searched for tidyFasta in the bioconductor manual (https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/manuals/MSstatsPTM/man/MSstatsPTM.pdf) and found the following two functions:
  1. locatePTM  
  2. MSstatsPTMSiteLocator  
Perhaps one of these could do what I need. These weren't mentioned in the bioconductor vignette so I wasn't aware they existed, but they look promising.


Kind regards,

Robin Colpaert

messages.subject: Re: peptide PTM annotation and sequence
parts:
Dear Tony,

In attach I added the annotation file and a subset of the data file. 

Note that I also needed to clean up/edit the data file a bit before MSstatsPTM could handle it, this is the code I use for that:
raw_data_EDIT$V12 = NULL
colnames(raw_data_EDIT) = raw_data_EDIT[1,]
raw_data_EDIT = raw_data_EDIT[-1,]

#remove rows without PTM, exclude 1st row which is part of the header
header_1 = raw_data_EDIT[1,]
raw_data_EDIT = raw_data_EDIT[!(raw_data_EDIT$X.9==""), ]
raw_data_EDIT = rbind(header_1, raw_data_EDIT)

#remove accessions that are not sp|UniProtID|geneID_MOUSE format
header_2 = raw_data_EDIT[2,]
raw_data_EDIT = raw_data_EDIT[ grepl("_MOUSE", raw_data_EDIT$X.10, fixed = TRUE),]    #gets rid of other species and CON-MOUSE
raw_data_EDIT = raw_data_EDIT[!grepl("*_sp", raw_data_EDIT$X.10, fixed = F),]         #gets rid of decoy hits (REV_sp)
raw_data_EDIT = rbind(header_1, header_2, raw_data_EDIT)

annotation_data_PTM = read.csv("phospho_annotation.csv", sep = ",")
msstatsPTM_input = ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat(raw_data_EDIT,
                                                annotation = annotation_data_PTM )
#renaming 1 column because name is wrong, this is due to ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat being an old converter
names(msstatsPTM_input$PTM)[names(msstatsPTM_input$PTM) == 'PeptideModifiedSequence'] <- 'PeptideSequence'

After these steps, I can run dataSummarizationPTM (with or without added total proteomics data).


Kind regards,

Robin

messages.subject: Re: peptide PTM annotation and sequence
parts:
Hi Robin,

So I played around with some functions and below is some code I put together so far that should help:

raw_data_EDIT$X.10 %>% unique() # print all unique proteins to search in uniprot for a FASTA file

raw_data_EDIT$X.10 = gsub("\\|.*","",gsub("sp\\|","", raw_data_EDIT$X.10)) # clean up protein name column to only contain uniprot ID

output = MSstatsPTMSiteLocator(raw_data_EDIT, protein_name_col = "X.10", unmod_pep_col = "X.8", mod_pep_col = "X.9", fasta_file = fasta_path, fasta_protein_name = "uniprot_ac")

The "output" table will contain a column called "Start" which indicates the starting index of the peptide sequence in the protein.  Since you also have information on the location of the PTM relative to the peptide sequence (column X.9), you can find the location of the PTM relative to the whole protein sequence.  

I saw the progenesis converter is an old converter, but I think we will look into updating it to contain the absolute location of the PTM so that these workarounds described here are not needed.

Tony
